*Initiation note, 14 October 2025. Rating: Buy. Current price: $42.10. 12-month price target: $58.*

## Thesis summary

We are initiating on Corvane Systems (NASDAQ: CRVN) with a Buy rating and a $58 price target, implying 37.8% upside from the current $42.10. Corvane sells ruggedized edge-compute gateways and the subscription software that manages them to logistics, utilities and discrete manufacturers. The market still values it as a hardware vendor at 11.5x EV/EBITDA and 18.2x P/E, but software is now 31% of revenue and rising, and we think the mix shift will carry EBITDA margins from 22.1% in FY2024 to 26.4% by FY2027. Corvane controls roughly 34% of the North American industrial edge-compute market, and that installed base is the moat. This is guaranteed upside for patient holders.

## Company snapshot

Corvane reported FY2024 revenue of $1,240 million, up 12.4% year on year, with a gross margin of 48.2%. The company has 82.4 million diluted shares outstanding and net debt of $342 million, for a market capitalisation of $3.47 billion and an enterprise value of $3.81 billion. Its largest customer, Halberd Logistics, accounted for 27% of FY2024 revenue under a contract that comes up for renewal on 31 March 2026.

Management has been disciplined with capital. CEO Dana Whitlock, who joined from a networking peer in 2022, cut the hardware SKU count by a third, moved field service to a partner model and started a $150 million buyback in May 2025, of which $61 million has been executed. Capital expenditure runs at about 3% of revenue, so most EBITDA converts to free cash flow, and the balance sheet can absorb a weak year without an equity raise.

## Why the market is mispricing CRVN

Sell-side coverage still models Corvane as a box vendor with lumpy shipment cycles. That framing made sense in 2021, when software was under 15% of revenue. It is perhaps less true today: each gateway now ships with a three-year management subscription, and renewal rates have averaged 96% across the installed base. Recurring revenue reached $384 million in FY2024, and we estimate it grows at roughly 22% per year through FY2027. As that stream compounds, earnings become more visible and the multiple should migrate toward software peers. It is important to note that none of this requires heroic hardware assumptions.

| FY2026E | 1,605 | 13.8% | 49.8% | 25.0% | $2.65 |
| FY2027E | 1,820 | 13.4% | 50.5% | 26.4% | $3.02 |

## Valuation

At $42.10, CRVN trades at 11.5x FY2025E EV/EBITDA of $331 million, 18.2x FY2025E EPS of $2.31 and a 6.1% free-cash-flow yield on FY2025E FCF of $212 million. Software-heavy industrial peers trade at 16–19x EV/EBITDA, while pure hardware peers sit near 9x. Our $58 price target applies a 20x multiple to FY2026E EPS of $2.65, which we think is conservative given a 0.85 PEG ratio and net leverage of just 1.0x EBITDA.

## Scenarios

- **Bull case ($74, 30% probability):** Software attach reaches 45% of new gateway shipments, EBITDA margin hits 28% in FY2027 and the market re-rates CRVN to 14x EV/EBITDA.
- **Base case ($58, 50% probability):** Our estimates above; the multiple expands modestly as software mix passes 35%.
- **Bear case ($31, 25% probability):** Hardware pricing compresses gross margin by 200 basis points and the multiple stays at 11.5x.

The probability-weighted value is $58.95, in line with our target.

## Catalysts

- **6 November 2025 — Q3 FY2025 results.** We expect software ARR above $410 million and a guidance raise.
- **9 December 2025 — Investor Day.** Management should unveil a FY2028 margin framework.
- **February 2026 — FY2026 guidance.** Consensus EPS of $2.52 looks too low against our $2.65.

## Key risks

- **Component supply:** Corvane single-sources its edge processors from one Taiwanese foundry partner; a disruption could delay shipments by a quarter.
- **Competition:** Larger industrial automation vendors could bundle edge gateways at low or zero margin.
- **Software execution:** Subscription churn has been low at 4% annually, but the sales force is still learning to sell recurring contracts.
- **Macro:** A slowdown in freight volumes would hit logistics customers first.

## Conclusion

Corvane will reach 30% EBITDA margins by FY2027 as software becomes the majority of gross profit. The stock is very cheap, and the market is simply missing the mix shift. Buy CRVN ahead of the Q3 print.
